speaker: Doctor
text: That is reassuring. Have you noticed any swelling in your face, lips, or tongue, or any difficulty breathing since the rash appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: The timing of the rash appearing after starting amoxicillin, combined with the distribution in the antecubital and popliteal fossae and generalized joint pain, strongly suggests serum sickness-like reaction. Have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes in your neck or armpits? REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_examination

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Serum Sickness-Like Reaction secondary to Amoxicillin. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_examination
